column10: 2026-10-25: first real forward PHREEQC REACTION-path titration, built as the complement to the real inverse-modeling attempts on file (run_phreeqc_inverse(), inverse_config.csv rows lst_sbw0001_sbrr_2026/lst_sbs0001_sbrr_2026) -- every one of which finds zero feasible solutions within PHREEQC's automatic mass-balance search (see ROADMAP.md Section 1/2, 2026-10-25). Target = sample 821 (SBW_0001, the real across-creek Lower Sinter Terrace well showing a clear, repeatable deviation above the fissure+SBRR conservative-mixing curve on calcite/dolomite SI). End-members = 816 (SBF_0001 fissure, real thermal) and 819 (SBRR, Steamboat Creek @ Rhodes Road, real conservative/dilution reference -- itself carries a modest real thermal signature, Cl=17.1 mg/L, T=59.4C, so this is a conservative not theoretically pure meteoric analog, same caveat as the mixing/inverse runs using this same pair). Mixing fraction (0.5714) is looked up automatically from the already-stored lst_fissure_sbrr_2026 mixing run (mixing_config.csv), not recomputed. step_min_mol/step_max_mol left blank so run_reaction_path_titration()'s own .estimate_reaction_bounds_mol() auto-sizes the range from the mixed fluid's real Ca/Mg/Alkalinity content (asymmetric: a real physical limit on the precipitation/negative side, a generous 6x-wider default on the dissolution/positive side, confirmed empirically 2026-10-25 to find a genuine interior RMSE minimum rather than an artifact at the range's own edge). Real result (scratch-DB verification, 2026-10-25): best-fit net reaction progress is a small net DISSOLUTION of calcite+dolomite (~+1.17e-4 mol combined), reducing the combined Ca/Mg/Alkalinity RMSE from ~45-48% (near-zero reaction progress, i.e. pure conservative mixing) to ~23% at the best fit -- a real, substantial improvement over pure mixing, but not a full reconciliation (consistent with -- not contradicting -- the inverse model's own finding that simple two-end-member-plus-carbonate mixing cannot fully explain SBW_0001's chemistry). Cl stays exactly conservative across every step (0.0000% variation), confirming the titration only moves carbonate species as intended.

2026-10-25 (follow-on): same forward REACTION-path titration method as the real SBW_0001 run (lst_sbw0001_forward_titration_2026), run here against SBS_0001 (sample 825, a real Lower Sinter Terrace spring) -- the concrete next step flagged in ROADMAP.md/manuscript/05_discussion_and_future_work.qmd once the SBW_0001 run was complete. Same end-members (816 fissure, 819 SBRR), same auto-estimated asymmetric bounds. Real stored mixing fraction for this target (0.8860, mixing_run_id 5) used automatically. Purpose: SBS_0001 sits much closer to the pure-conservative-mixing curve than SBW_0001 on the forward_mixing_model_validation.png figure, so this checks whether it needs little/no reaction correction (as that figure alone suggests) or a smaller but still real signal of its own.
2026-10-25 (follow-on): same method, target = SBS_0002 (sample 820, a real Lower Sinter Terrace seep). Real stored mixing fraction 0.7744 (mixing_run_id 5).

2026-10-25 (follow-on): same method, target = SBS_0003 (sample 822, a real Lower Sinter Terrace spring, the lowest-elevation real downgradient target on this flowpath). Real stored mixing fraction 0.8521 (mixing_run_id 5).

2026-10-25 (follow-on): tests whether adding Anhydrite (CaSO4) as a candidate phase resolves SBS_0001's real tension -- its own observed chemistry has the highest SO4 (187 mg/L) and lowest Alkalinity (195 mg/L) of the four real downgradient targets, the classic gypsum/anhydrite signature a calcite/dolomite-only titration cannot produce (it ties Ca directly to carbonate, not sulfate). SBS_0001's own already-computed Anhydrite SI (-1.19) is among the least-undersaturated of the six real flowpath samples, physically plausible room for this dissolution. Same end-members as the baseline run (lst_sbs0001_forward_titration_2026): fissure(816)+SBRR(819).

2026-10-25 (follow-on): same hypothesis as the Anhydrite row, but Gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O) instead -- the more soluble, lower-temperature-stable hydrate form. Tests whether the less-stable form fits SBS_0001's real chemistry better.

2026-10-25 (follow-on): combined test per explicit user request ('and maybe Fluorite, given real F data') -- Anhydrite plus Fluorite (CaF2) together. SBS_0001 has real F=1.52 mg/L and Fluorite SI=-2.91 (more undersaturated than Anhydrite/Gypsum, a weaker but still real candidate).

2026-10-25 (follow-on): tests the ALTERNATE hypothesis that SBS_0001 mixes with a different, higher-sulfate shallow water than the other three real LST targets, rather than needing an extra mineral phase. Meteoric end-member = sample 919 (Tick Spr., Mariner & Janik 1995) -- real chemistry (SO4=143, Ca=100, Cl=48, Alkalinity=210 mg/L), notably higher SO4/Ca than SBRR or Jumbo Grade Spring, but -- same documented limitation as Jumbo Grade Spring -- NO coordinate on file, so its real geographic position relative to SBS_0001 is unconfirmed. Phases kept at the baseline Calcite;Dolomite to isolate the end-member-choice effect from the phase-choice effect tested in the three rows above. Mixing fraction computed fresh (no stored mixing run exists for this pair).

2026-10-25 (follow-on): same alternate-meteoric-end-member test, using the other previously-identified real candidate, sample 920 (Jumbo Gr. S., Mariner & Janik 1995, SO4=68, Ca=95, Cl=7, Alkalinity=375 mg/L) -- also no coordinate on file. Run alongside the Tick Spring row above for a real side-by-side comparison of both candidates against the SBRR baseline.

2026-10-25 (follow-on): first forward titration run with SBW_0002 (815, resort tank) as the TARGET rather than only as an alternate thermal end-member elsewhere in this project. SBW_0002 has complete real chemistry and an already-stored mixing fraction of 1.043 against fissure(816)+SBRR(819) -- slightly ABOVE 1.0, a real, already-documented (Session 30) edge case (SBW_0002 is the one real sample found to be more concentrated than the thermal reference itself), not a new problem introduced here. Same phases as the SBW_0001/springs baseline runs.

2026-10-25 (follow-on): COMBINED test of both hypotheses together for SBS_0001 -- Anhydrite+Fluorite phases AND the Tick Spring (919) alternate meteoric end-member. Real result: 35.7% combined RMSE, WORSE than Tick Spring alone with the baseline Calcite;Dolomite phases (33.4%, the single best real result across all seven SBS_0001 variants tested) -- the two improvements do not simply stack. Tick Spring's own real chemistry already explains part of what the sulfate phases were trying to add, so combining them does not help further.
